subject.title: [Bug]: Kimi Coding auth fallback in systemd Gateway when config env is not injected

question: Should `openclaw.json` `env.KIMI_API_KEY` remain a supported durable auth source for systemd-managed Gateway turns, or should daemon provider keys be required to live in `~/.openclaw/.env` or per-agent auth profiles?
rationale: Current code, docs, and reporter logs point at a credential-contract boundary rather than a single mechanical missing import; choosing the intended source of truth affects auth semantics, status output, service env persistence, and docs.

options.title: Support config env for managed Gateway
options.body: Keep the documented Kimi config-env path valid and add runtime/status/service-env tests or warnings proving systemd Gateway turns resolve it consistently.

options.title: Require daemon env/auth profiles
options.body: Change docs and `models status` wording/JSON so config env is not presented as effective managed-Gateway auth, and steer users to `~/.openclaw/.env` or per-agent auth profiles.

options.title: Fold into broader env unification
options.body: Treat this issue as the Kimi-specific reproducer while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/90270 owns the broader env-source precedence redesign.

recommendation.title: Support config env for managed Gateway
recommendation.body: Keep the documented Kimi config-env path valid and add runtime/status/service-env tests or warnings proving systemd Gateway turns resolve it consistently.

likelyOwner.reason: The current blame and recent refactor history span the config snapshot, service-env, and model-status surfaces that need a contract decision.
